patches.old_text:
## Payment method priority

Stripe uses the first available in this order:

| Priority | Source | API field |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Invoice default PM | `invoice.default_payment_method` |
| 2 | Subscription default PM | `subscription.default_payment_method` |
| 3 | Customer invoice default PM | `customer.invoice_settings.default_payment_method` |
| 4 | (Legacy) Customer default source | `customer.default_source` |
patches.new_text:
## Saved-default payment method fallback

For invoice collection, Stripe uses the first available saved default in this order; accepted payment method **types** are configured separately with `payment_settings.payment_method_types`:

| Priority | Saved default | API field |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Invoice | `invoice.default_payment_method` |
| 2 | Subscription | `subscription.default_payment_method` |
| 3 | Customer or customer-configured Account | `customer.invoice_settings.default_payment_method` or `configuration.customer.billing.default_payment_method`, respectively |
| 4 | Legacy customer source | `customer.default_source` |

See [[source-stripe-subscriptions-invoices]] (2026-11-07 capture, lines 62–71) for the fallback and [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]] for accepted types.
patches.reason: Distinguish the saved-default fallback from accepted method types and include the newly documented Account field.

patches.old_text: **Pause for review**: set `auto_advance=false` within 1h → prevents auto-finalization. Resume with `auto_advance=true`.
patches.new_text: **Pause for review**: set `auto_advance=false` within one hour of `invoice.created` to prevent automatic payment attempts and invoice emailing while reviewing. Resume automatic collection with `auto_advance=true`. The cited invoice-guide passage does not expressly establish a finalization outcome; see [[source-stripe-subscriptions-invoices]] (2026-05-13 lines 234–242; 2026-11-07 lines 263–271).
patches.reason: Both captures expressly describe payment and email suppression, whereas the concept's finalization claim exceeds this evidence.

patches.new_text: | `invoice.subscription_details.metadata` | Contains subscription metadata from invoice creation, even if subscription metadata changes later; see [[source-stripe-subscriptions-invoices]] (2026-05-13 line 280; 2026-11-07 line 309) |
patches.reason: Retain supported creation-time snapshot semantics without asserting blanket immutability.

patches.old_text: **`save_default_payment_method`**: when enabled, whatever PM the customer pays with becomes the new subscription default.
patches.new_text: **`save_default_payment_method`**: set `payment_settings.save_default_payment_method=on_subscription` to save the method from a successful subscription payment as `subscription.default_payment_method`; the default is `off`. This subscription setting is separate from the Dashboard **Save customer payment information** setting. See [[source-stripe-subscriptions-invoices]] (2026-11-07 lines 73–77).
patches.reason: Narrow saving to the documented successful-payment condition and opt-in setting.

patches.old_text: `payment_settings.payment_method_types` overrides which PMs the customer can use for a specific subscription (e.g. `['card', 'customer_balance']`). Passed to the subscription's SetupIntent and invoices.
patches.new_text: `payment_settings.payment_method_types` limits allowed **types**, not the identity of a saved default method. An explicit subscription list overrides Invoice default type configuration for that subscription and passes to its SetupIntent and invoices. With `send_invoice`, customers choose eligible types on the Hosted Invoice Page; with `charge_automatically`, Stripe attempts payment without first showing a selector. Eligibility also depends on account activation, currency, amount, country, collection method, and product support. [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]]
patches.reason: November clarifies type identity, collection flow and invoice eligibility.

patches.old_text: **Pitfall**: if a `default_payment_method` is set on the customer or subscription, it must be included in `payment_method_types` or it won't be used and payment may fail.
patches.new_text: **Pitfall**: when an applicable default payment method exists, include its **type** in an explicit `payment_method_types` list; otherwise that default method cannot pay the subscription's invoices. This type allowance is separate from the priority of an individual saved method. [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]]
patches.reason: New warning names method type and invoice consequence precisely.

patches.old_text: **`save_default_payment_method`**: when enabled, whatever PM the customer pays with becomes the new subscription default.
patches.new_text: **Save-default controls (May 2026 capture)**: the guide says Dashboard Invoice **Save customer payment information** or Subscription `payment_settings.save_default_payment_method` can make a method used to pay an invoice “the new default.” It does not identify the destination object for each control. The November payment-method-types capture is silent on saving behavior; see [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]].
patches.reason: Prior approved review rejects the unsupported claim that both controls save to subscription.default_payment_method.
warnings: May-only; no destination object established for both controls by assigned captures.

patches.old_text: **Payment update links** (Dashboard, `charge_automatically` only): single-use, card-only, 30-day expiry, `active`/`past_due`/`trialing` status required, doesn't change customer default PM.
patches.new_text: **Payment update links (May 2026 capture)**: the Dashboard guide described links for automatically billed `active`, `past_due`, or `trialing` subscriptions; card-only, one use, 30-day expiry. They update the associated subscription's method, not the customer's default. The November type-settings guide does not address link availability. [[source-stripe-subscriptions-payment-methods-setting]]
patches.reason: Preserve May link restrictions with date and keep distinct from save-default controls.
warnings: November omission does not establish current availability or deprecation.
